mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods following a month with FEDFUNDS < 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three months signals labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within five trading days due to reduced consumer spending confidence.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months but 5-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: Both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 2% in 2 months but 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO > 1.5% YoY) signals robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO YoY growth > 1.5% but 20-day SPX returns are negative in more than 55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales growth (RSAFS) indicates resilient consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through sustained corporate revenue momentum.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth > 2% in month but 5-day SPX returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation above 3.5% annualized signals persistent price pressures, prompting delayed monetary easing and negative S&P 500 returns within five trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL annualized rate > 3.5% but 5-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days via reduced household income.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth negative and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in month but 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS above 4.0% signals active monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and suppressing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% but 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of periods.
